newsitem.title: CANADA: Integrated oils lead Canadian energy stocks upward.
newsitem.headline: Integrated oils lead Canadian energy stocks upward.

text.p: Canadian energy stocks surged higher on Tuesday with integrated oil companies leading the pack amid strong oil and gasoline prices and a rosy outlook for earnings and cash flow, analysts said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's oil and gas subindex soared 144.19 points to an all-time high 7,223.15 late in Tuesday's session.
Canada's biggest three integrateds -- Imperial Oil Ltd, Shell Canada Ltd and Petro-Canada -- led the price jumps with major increases.
Imperial climbed 2.45 to 74.25, Shell Canada was up 2.25 to 25 and Petro-Canada rose 0.85 to 25.50.

Suncor Energy Inc, whose results are less dependent on refining and marketing than its peers, was down 0.20 to 46.55. But Suncor surged C$8.30 last week after the company unveiled a C$2.2 billion plan to more than double its oil sands plant's output over five years.

The integrateds already reported their strongest first-half operating results, surpassing previous highs of 1985. Full-year returns were expected to be their best ever, said Terry Peters, analyst with Leowen Ondaatje McCutcheon.
Peters said the downstream operations, which usually pump out strong cash flow in August because of high demand for gasoline, were responsible for even more of the excitement than usual.
That was because refining and marketing margins continued to outshine last year's when the companies were hammered by retail gasoline price wars, especially in Quebec.
Also this year, a recent series of refinery maintenance shutdowns in the United States was responsible for a big draw on gasoline stocks which was sending prices upward, analysts said.
Contributing to better shareholder returns for Imperial and Shell were stock buybacks, with the two companies writing checks for a combined C$2.4 billion in one-time deals over the past two years.
Imperial has meanwhile maintained its continuing issuer bid program.

Yield investors were impressed by Shell Canada's increase in its quarterly dividend which accompanied record results last week, Peters said, adding that the move also highlighted the firm's financial strength. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
